To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optical properties of the micromachined reflectors can be improved by reducing the size of the etch holes.
the optical properties of etch holes on surface-micromachine mirrors are wavelength and incident angle dependent and can be used to tune the optical properties of microreflective mirrors.
etch holes have a great influence in the optical properties of mirrors realized using surface micromachning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties of microreflecting surfaces realized using the MUMPS process.
the optical properties of the microreflectors and their application in optical microsystems.
the influence of etch holes on the optical properties (reflectivity) of surface micromached mirrors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
etch holes are not a good choice for the realization of surface micromirrors with a high reflectance.
etch holes have a great influence upon the optical properties of microreflecting surfaces, especially in the case of a large dimension of etch-hole array.
the reflectivity of surface-micronachined mirrors is a function of both the incident angle and the dimension of etched holes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reflectivity of surface-micrmachined mirrors with large etch holes can be as low as 50%, while the reflectivity of the mirrors without any etch holes is close to 100%.
the etch holes should be minimized in the surface micromanufacturing process for optical applications.
the optical properties of the surface micromached mirrors depend strongly on the dimension of etched holes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when designing microreflectors with a high reflectivity and a high efficiency, etch holes should be avoided or minimized in the design.
etch holes should be avoided or reduced in number when the optical properties of mirrors are critical.
the optical properties of microreflective surfaces are strongly dependent on the size of the etch holes and their distribution.
